newsitem.title: USA: Review NAFTA impact -- next US House ag chairman.
newsitem.headline: Review NAFTA impact -- next US House ag chairman.

text.p: Oregon Republican Bob Smith, tabbed to be chairman of the U.S. House Agriculture Committee, said Wednesday he wanted to "revisit NAFTA" due to complaints of unfairly priced Mexican cattle and Canadian grain.
"I want to determine what is happening in the market place," Smith said in an interview with Reuters.

Smith said the North American Free Trade Agreement included language to protect farmers and ranchers from unfair practices. There are plenty of "disgruntled people" in farm country, he said, so he wanted to take a look at how well the agreement among Canada, Mexico and United States was working.
Smith said the federal government was mismanaging national forests in the Northwest and allowing a buildup of dead trees.
"We have a fuel load on the forest floor that is so heavy...you can't hardly fight a fire," he said.
Congressional attention must be given to the situation in the Northwest and the policies that caused it, he said.
Smith said he wanted amicable relations with Democrats on the committee.

Now 65, Smith retired in 1994 after a decade in the House. When he agreed to run again, Republican leaders said he would retain seniority to be in line for the Agriculture Committee chairmanship. Party members will meet in a few weeks to formally select their leaders.

Before election to Congress in 1982, Smith was a cattle rancher and 22-year veteran of the Oregon Legislature. He was critical of European farm subsidies and opposed what Republicans came to call the "war on the West" -- attempts to raise grazing fees and limit logging.
He represents agriculturally dominated eastern Oregon.
